ideas: Older colleagues share experience and practical advice
Same-age colleagues are easier to communicate with
Mixed-age teams balance fresh ideas and wisdom

phrases.meaning: learn how a job is done
not make errors that cost a lot
a new way of seeing things

model: I prefer working with people who are older than me. First, they have years of experience, which helps me learn the ropes much faster. For example, when I started my current job in logistics, there was a senior colleague who'd been in the industry for fifteen years, and whenever I got stuck, I could pick his brain. His advice helped me avoid costly mistakes that I definitely would have made on my own. Another reason is that older colleagues often give more honest advice about my career path. They've been through the same stages, so they can tell me which skills are really worth developing. At the moment, I'm meeting one of them for coffee every month, and those chats are more useful than any online course. Of course, people my own age are easier to bounce ideas off, and they bring a fresh perspective, so I'm not saying they're less valuable. But overall, for someone who's still early in their career, I think older colleagues are the better teachers.
